items.article: The Gears of War: E-Day campaign is one of the series' very best, telling the story of where it all began, but the open-world sections are a disappoin Gears of War: E-Day is absolutely relentless. Set during Emergence Day, the name given to the moment the Locust Horde invaded the planet Sera (referenced repeatedly in previous games), this is a prequel to everything we know about Gears of War. For the entire duration of its 20+-hour runtime, you hardly have a moment to breathe. Taking place across three in-game days, E-Day gives you control of whichever member of Bravo squad takes your fancy: squad leader Marcus Fenix, the iconic Dominic Santiago, cadet Lucas Reyes, or thought-she'd-retired Mags Carter. The four are tasked with repelling the Locust army in any way possible, rescuing survivors, and helping what remains of civilization get back on its feet. As you'd expect when defending against a surprise invasion by a species you didn't even know existed that threatens all of humanity, Gears of War: E-Day is frantic. So, does their colour indicate differences in behaviour, health or survival? First, colour does not make a white pigeon a different species from a grey one. “White and grey pigeons are colour variations of the same species, Columba livia. They can interbreed freely and produce fertile offspring, which is evidence of their common species origin,” says Dr Sharma. Pigeons can display considerable variation in plumage, ranging from the familiar grey and darker patterns to predominantly white birds. “White pigeons are often observed to be less territorially competent and more concentrated in city centres,” says Dr Sharma.

items.text: Section 163 imposed in Delhi: What it means amid protest in Jantar Mantar against CEC Gyanesh Kumar
items.article: Delhi Police has imposed Section 163 across New Delhi ahead of a proposed Jantar Mantar protest against CEC Gyanesh Kumar today. The order bars gatherings of five or more without permission, demonstrations, slogans and certain items. Security has been tightened amid expectations of a large turnout. Delhi Police on Friday imposed prohibitory orders under Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) across the New Delhi district, ahead of the proposed protest at Jantar Mantar against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. The order prohibits public gatherings of five or more people, demonstrations and other activities without prior written permission. The police have denied permission for the demonstration, scheduled for 11 am today, on Gandhi Jayanti. The protest has been called by the All India Students’ Association (AISA), Rajya Sabha MP Manoj Jha, and Supreme Court lawyer Prashant Bhushan. Under the order, public gatherings or assemblies of five or more people, processions, demonstrations, picketing and dharnas are prohibited without prior written permission. Section 163 empowers an Executive Magistrate to issue orders in urgent cases posing a threat to public safety or order, allowing temporary restrictions on public gatherings without prior written permission. The orders were imposed to prevent public gatherings and demonstrations amid planned protests against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, which the police have denied permission for.
